summary: The S&P 500 fell a modest 0.25% today to 7,711, but the real story was Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh's speech at Jackson Hole, where he warned that inflation is not slowing fast enough and left the door open to raising interest rates. That spooked tech stocks hard, with the Nasdaq 100 dropping 0.65%, while gold fell 2.19% and bitcoin dropped 3.37% as the dollar strengthened. Canada's economy grew a strong 3.3% annualized in the second quarter, a bright spot for the Canadian side of the portfolio. Next week brings earnings from DELL on September 1 and AVGO on September 2.
